I found the most unnecessarily suspicious website ever. 😂

It's called **CreepyLink**.

You give it a normal URL, and it turns it into a link that looks like you're about to download a virus or get your account hacked.

Completely unnecessary.

Absolutely hilarious.

🔗 [CreepyLink](https://creepylink.com/)

Would you click it if a friend sent it to you? 😂

#Internet #Technology #WebDevelopment #Developers

I have spent two years building with AI, and the honeymoon phase is over.

Most people think vibe coding is about prompting until the code works. But I realized that if you are just patching AI-generated errors, you are not building, you are just fixing someone else's mess.

Here is what I learned about building apps fast without losing my mind.

Context is everything. Do not dump your entire project into the prompt. Break it down. Give the AI specific files and clear constraints. If you cannot describe the problem, the AI cannot solve it.

Know when to walk away. If I have asked for a fix three times and it is still broken, I delete it. Trying to untangle AI-generated spaghetti code is a trap. Sometimes, the cleanest solution is a fresh start.

Security is not an optional add-on. The AI will write code that runs perfectly but leaves your database wide open. Authentication, API keys, and validation are your job, not the machine's.

Most importantly, vibe coding did not stop me from learning. It shifted my mindset from saying I do not know how to build something, to admitting I do not know how to build it yet. That slight change in perspective is why I ship more projects today than I did two years ago.

You still have to be the engineer. AI is just a tool that makes the process faster, not a replacement for your technical judgment.

What is the one thing you refuse to let AI handle when you are building?

#vibecoding #developer #softwaredevelopment #buildinginpublic

The next 30 seconds will teach you what 2 years of vibe coding taught me.

I've spent the last two years using AI to build apps, websites, and random ideas that probably would've taken me weeks or months to build before.

I've used Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and plenty of other tools.

Here's what I've learned:

1. Context is everything.

The AI is only as good as the context you give it.
Don't throw your entire codebase at it and hope for the best. Give it the relevant files, explain what you're trying to achieve, and keep your project rules and requirements documented.

2. Be specific.

"Build me a cool website" will probably give you something that looks cool for about 5 minutes.
Break the problem down.
Tell it exactly what you want, what you already have, what constraints it needs to follow, and what the final result should do.

3. Know when to stop prompting.

If I've asked AI to fix the same problem three times and it's still broken, I stop.
Sometimes the best solution is to delete the broken component and rebuild it from scratch.
Trying to patch AI-generated spaghetti code forever is a trap.

4. Don't confuse vibe coding with not coding.

You still need to understand what you're building.
You need to read the code, understand errors, test things, make architectural decisions, and know when the AI is confidently doing something stupid.
AI can write the code.
You still have to be the engineer.

5. Security is your responsibility.

AI will happily generate code that works but isn't necessarily secure.
Validations, authentication, permissions, webhooks, database rules, API keys...
Don't assume the AI handled them correctly just because the app works.

6. Building fast doesn't mean building the right thing.

Vibe coding makes it incredibly easy to turn an idea into a working prototype.
But if the idea itself is bad, you've just built the wrong thing faster.
Validate what you're building before spending hours building it.

7. The biggest lesson:

Vibe coding hasn't made me stop learning how to code.
It has made me more willing to build things I would've previously thought were too difficult.
I've gone from:
"I don't know how to build this."
to:
"I don't know how to build this yet. Let me figure it out."
And I think that's the real power of it.

Don't let AI replace your thinking. Use it to expand what you can build.

What has vibe coding taught you?
